title: Second Syrian Republic
capsule: The Second Syrian Republic was established following the end of the French Mandate in April 1946 and formally reconstituted under the Syrian Constitution of 1950. The republic was dominated by military coups — Husni al-Za'im's March 1949 putsch, the first in the post-war Arab world, was followed by two further coups before civilian rule briefly returned. Adib al-Shishakli's dictatorship (1951–1954) and the subsequent return to constitutional government culminated in the 1958 union with Egypt, forming the United Arab Republic under Gamal Abdel Nasser, driven by pan-Arab sentiment following the Suez Crisis. Syria withdrew from the union after a September 1961 coup and the republic was reconstituted briefly before the Ba'athist coup of 8 March 1963 ended the republican period.
